Rashi on Chullin 41b:10:1.hebrew: זה הכלל - בגמ' מפרש לאתויי מאי, דהא חשבינהו לכולהו:
Rashi on Chullin 41b:10:1.english: This is the rule - The Gemara will explain what this comes to include, since it [the mishna] has already enumerated all of them [explicitly].

Rashi on Chullin 41b:11:1.english: Is it subject to vowing and donation? - This is [asked] as a question.

Rashi on Chullin 41b:11:2.hebrew: בכל יום - שבכל יום הוא עומד בספק חטאת, ולבו נוקפו שמא חטא. ומצינו שהכשיר הכתוב אשם תלוי ליקרב וליאכל היכא דהוחזק ספק חטא בעדים, והאי נמי אנן סהדי דכל יומא בספק חטא קאי:
Rashi on Chullin 41b:11:2.english: Every day - For every day he stands in a state of doubt about a sin offering, and his heart troubles him that perhaps he sinned. And we find that the verse permitted a provisional guilt offering to be offered and eaten where a doubtful sin was established by witnesses; and here too, we ourselves are witnesses that every day he stands in a state of doubt about a sin.

Rashi on Chullin 41b:12:1.hebrew: זימנא קביעא ליה - בערב הפסח. הלכך, מידע ידעי דדברי רוח הן:
Rashi on Chullin 41b:12:1.english: Its time is fixed - On the eve of Passover. Therefore, they certainly know that [such statements] are words of wind, i.e., empty talk.

Rashi on Chullin 41b:12:2.hebrew: הואיל והפרשתו כל השנה - כל ימות השנה ראוי להפרישו ולהניחו עד זמנו. הלכך השתא נמי אמרי דיכול להתנדב, השתא מפריש ליה, וקשחיט פסח בשאר ימות השנה — וקי"ל דשלמים הוא — ואמרי שהוא קשחיט שלמים בחוץ ואכיל להו:
Rashi on Chullin 41b:12:2.english: Since its designation [is] throughout the year - All the days of the year it is fit to designate it and to leave it until its time. Therefore, now too they would say [that one may bring it as a vow or gift]: now he designates it, and when he slaughters a Paschal offering during the other days of the year — and we hold that it is a peace offering — they would say that he is slaughtering peace offerings outside [the Temple court] and eating them.

Rashi on Chullin 41b:13:1.hebrew: מידע ידיע - דמשקר, ולא נפיק חורבה מיניה:
Rashi on Chullin 41b:13:1.english: He surely knows - That he is lying in his declaration, and no ruin comes out of it.

Rashi on Chullin 41b:13:2.hebrew: דרמי מידי אמומא - שיהא נכסה בצמר או בטיט, ולא חזו ליה, וסברי תם הוא:
Rashi on Chullin 41b:13:2.english: That an item is cast over the blemish - That it would be covered with wool or with mud, and they do not see it, and they think it is unblemished.

Rashi on Chullin 41b:14:1.hebrew: לא שנו אלא שאינו מחוייב חטאת - דלא אמרי אינשי: השתא מפריש לה, דהא חטאת לאו בנדר ובנדבה אתי. והא לא חשו רבנן דלמא מאן דחזי סבר מחוייב חטאת הוא, דההוא קלא אית ליה, דמי שבא לידו דבר עבירה בשוגג אינו מחפה עליה, כדי שיתבייש ומתכפר לו:
Rashi on Chullin 41b:14:1.english: They taught this only where he is not obligated to bring a sin offering - For people will not say, “Now he is setting it aside,” since a sin offering does not come by vow or by freewill offering. Now, the Gemara could have asked: But the Rabbis did not worry that perhaps one who sees will think that he is obligated to bring a sin offering. The answer is that this has a reputation of being embarrassing, for one to whom a matter of sin came in an unintentional manner does not cover it up, so that he will be embarrassed and be atoned for.

Rashi on Chullin 41b:14:2.hebrew: אבל מחוייב חטאת - מאן דחזי סבר, לשם חטאת הוא מפרישה עכשיו:
Rashi on Chullin 41b:14:2.english: But one who is liable for a sin offering - Whoever sees [him] will think that he is now setting it aside for the sake of a sin offering.

Rashi on Chullin 41b:14:3.hebrew: והא לא קאמר לשם חטאתי - דמשמע "שאני חייב". אלא "לשם חטאת" דמשמע לשון נדר, ומידע ידיע דאין בדבריו כלום. דבשלמא דבר הנידר ונידב, איכא למימר: השתא מקבל לה עליה בשעת הפרשה, ולא בעי למימר "לשם עולתי". אבל הכא, כל כמה דלא אמר "לשם חטאתי", לא משמע "לשם אותה שאני מחוייב":
Rashi on Chullin 41b:14:3.english: But he did not say "for the sake of my sin offering" - Which would imply "that I am obligated." But "for the sake of a sin offering" implies the language of a vow, and it is well known that there is nothing in his words. For granted, with regard to an item that can be vowed or donated, one can say: Now he is accepting it upon himself at the time of designation, and he need not say "for the sake of my burnt offering." But here, as long as he did not say "for the sake of my sin offering," it does not imply "for the sake of that [sin offering] which I am obligated [to bring]."

Rashi on Chullin 41b:14:4.hebrew: באומר לשם חטאתי - והיכא דאינו מחוייב חטאת, אפי' אם [אמר] לשם חטאתי — מידע ידעי דמשקר:
Rashi on Chullin 41b:14:4.english: Where he says: For the sake of my sin offering - But where he is not liable to bring a sin offering, even if he said "for the sake of my sin offering," people know that he is lying.

Rashi on Chullin 41b:15:1.hebrew: שאין לו זבח - דליכא למימר השתא עביד לה תמורה, דבמאי מימר לה? דהא ליכא למיגזר. מאן דחזי סבר: יש לו זבח אחר, דההוא קלא אית ליה:
Rashi on Chullin 41b:15:1.english: That he has no offering - For it cannot be said that he is now making it a substitute, for with what would he be substituting it? For there is nothing to decree [about]. Whoever sees [him] thinks: He has another offering, since he has that [other] voice, i.e., that report [of its existence].

Rashi on Chullin 41b:15:2.hebrew: אימר אמורי אמיר ביה - ומאן דחזי סבר: השתא מימר לה בהך אמירה דבשעת שחיטה. ואע"ג דלא מוקי לה בהדי זבח, חייל עלה שם תמורה, דתנן בתמורה (דף כז.): ״תחת חטאת, תחת עולה שיש לי בבית״ — היה לו, דבריו קיימין:
Rashi on Chullin 41b:15:2.english: Say that he is substituting it - And one who sees [this] thinks: Now he is substituting it [for his sacrifice] by this statement made at the time of slaughter. And even though he did not designate it alongside the sacrificial animal, the status of a substitute takes effect upon it, as we learned in Temurah (27a): [If one said,] "In place of a sin offering," or "in place of a burnt offering that I have at home," and he had [one], his words stand.

Rashi on Chullin 41b:15:3.hebrew: והא לא קאמר לשם תמורת זבחי - דלהוי משמע שימירנה בו, אלא "לשם תמורה", דמשמע דבשמא בעלמא בעי לשוויי תמורה, ואיהו ליתא. אלא היכא דמימר לה בזבח, דתנן בתמורה (שם): תחת חטאת, תחת עולה — לא אמר כלום:
Rashi on Chullin 41b:15:3.english: But he did not say "for the sake of a substitute for my offering" - [He did not say it] in a way that would imply that he is substituting this animal for it; rather, [he said only] "for the sake of a substitute," which implies that he merely wishes to designate a substitute by name alone, and that [substitute] does not exist. Rather, [a substitution takes effect] only where he substitutes it for an [actual] offering, as we learned in Temurah (there): [If one says] "in place of a sin offering" or "in place of a burnt offering," he has said nothing.

Rashi on Chullin 41b:15:4.hebrew: לשם תמורת זבחי - ואשמועינן מתני' דהיכא דאין לו זבח, כשרה, ולא חיישינן דלמא מאן דחזי סבר דאית ליה. מ"ט? דאי הוה ליה, מידע הוו ידעי:
Rashi on Chullin 41b:15:4.english: For the sake of a substitute for my offering - And the Mishnah teaches us that where he has no offering, [the slaughter] is valid, and we are not concerned that perhaps whoever sees [him] will think that he has one. What is the reason? Because if he had one, [people] would have known [it].

Rashi on Chullin 41b:16:1.hebrew: עולת נזיר - דאי אמר הריני שוחט לשם עולת נזיר, פסולה, דמאן דחזי סבר נדר הוא, והשתא קמפריש ושחיט לה. ואע"ג דנזיר נידר ונידב הוא — דע"י נדר הוא בא — אי לא הוה תני זה הכלל לאתויי, לא שמעינן ליה מעולה דרישא:
Rashi on Chullin 41b:16:1.english: The burnt offering of a nazirite - For if he said, "I am slaughtering for the sake of the burnt offering of a nazirite," it is disqualified, because whoever sees [him] thinks it is a vow, and that now he is setting [the animal] aside and slaughtering it. And even though a nazirite is [both] a vow and a voluntary gift — since it comes by means of a vow — if [the mishna] had not taught "this is the principle" to add [something], we would not have learned it from the burnt offering in the first clause.

Rashi on Chullin 41b:16:2.hebrew: דמהו דתימא - ליכא למיחש שמא יאסר לחורבה, דמידע ידעי דהא לא נדר:
Rashi on Chullin 41b:16:2.english: For lest you say - There is no need to be concerned about the ruin [of the animal's being forbidden], for they know that he did not vow.

Rashi on Chullin 41b:17:1.hebrew: קא משמע לן - דמימר אמרי, דלמא נדר בצינעא זה שלשים יום, שהוא סתם נזירות, ובשלשים יום לא מינכרא מילתיה לשכניו:
Rashi on Chullin 41b:17:1.english: It teaches us - For they might say: Perhaps he vowed in private [to be a nazirite] thirty days ago, which is an unspecified nazirite vow [that lasts thirty days]; and within thirty days his matter is not noticeable to his neighbors.

Rashi on Chullin 41b:17:2.hebrew: לאתויי עולת יולדת - שאם אמר לשם עולת יולדת בפירוש, כשרה, דמידע ידעי דהשתא לא נדר לה, וכדמפרש בשאין לו אשה:
Rashi on Chullin 41b:17:2.english: To include the burnt offering of a woman after childbirth - For if one said explicitly [that he slaughters] for the sake of a woman's post-childbirth burnt offering, [the slaughter] is valid, since it is known that she is not now bringing it as a vow, as [the Gemara] explains in [the chapter beginning] "One who has no wife."

Rashi on Chullin 41b:1:1.hebrew: יחקה את הצדוקים - יחזיק ידיהם בחוקותיהם. יחקה לשון חוק:
Rashi on Chullin 41b:1:1.english: He would imitate the Sadducees - He would support their hands in their statutes. "Yachkeh" is an expression of "chok" (statute):

Rashi on Chullin 41b:2:1.english: Into a reflection - His own image, which is seen in the water:

Rashi on Chullin 41b:2:2.english: Turbid - A reflection is not discernible in them.

Rashi on Chullin 41b:3:1.hebrew: והאמרת אין שוחטין לגומא - והדר תני אבל עושה גומא:
Rashi on Chullin 41b:3:1.english: But you said one may not slaughter into a pit - And then he taught: "But he may make a pit."

Rashi on Chullin 41b:5:1.english: At all - Even in a house [is it forbidden to slaughter into a pit], because it appears like the practice of the Sadducees.

Rashi on Chullin 41b:6:1.english: On the sides of the boat - [Meaning the blood flows] from the sides of the boat to the water.

Rashi on Chullin 41b:7:3.english: And in the marketplace he should not do so - Because a person is not concerned about clearing out the marketplace [of the blood].

Rashi on Chullin 41b:7:4.english: Investigation after him - Lest he be a heretic [given over] to idol worship, and so people will distance themselves from his bread and his wine.

Rashi on Chullin 41b:8:1.english: One who slaughters - Non-sacred animals outside [the Temple courtyard].

Rashi on Chullin 41b:8:2.hebrew: לשם עולה - דכיון דבאה בנדר ובנדבה, הרואה אומר עכשיו הוא מקדיש ושוחטה לעולה, וקדשים בחוץ מותרים, וגזור רבנן עליה פסול, וכן שלמים וכו':
Rashi on Chullin 41b:8:2.english: For the sake of a burnt-offering - Since [a burnt-offering] can come through a vow or a freewill-offering, an onlooker will say, "He is consecrating it right now, and slaughtering it as a burnt-offering," and [will conclude] that consecrated animals may be slaughtered outside [the Temple courtyard]. The Sages therefore decreed that it is invalid [to eat] - and so too with peace-offerings, etc.

Rashi on Chullin 41b:8:3.hebrew: אשם תלוי - בא על ספק חיוב כרת, כגון ב' חתיכות לפניו ואכל אחת מהן, ובאו עדים ואמרו אחת מהן של חלב היתה ואין ידוע איזו אכל; אשתו ואחותו עמו בבית, כסבור שבא על אשתו ונחלף, ולא ידע למחר על איזו מהם בא, שהיו שתיהן במטה והוא לא היה יודע - מביא אשם תלוי להגין מן היסורין, עד שיודע לו אם חטא ודאי מביא חטאת. ובגמ' פריך: והא לאו נידר ונידב הוא, והרואה יודע שאין בדבריו כלום, שאין שם אשם תלוי אא"כ היה מחוייב, וההוא קלא אית ליה. ופסח נמי בגמ' פריך:
Rashi on Chullin 41b:8:3.english: A suspended guilt-offering - This comes on account of a doubt of liability for karet, such as: two pieces of meat were before him and he ate one of them, and witnesses then came and said that one of them was forbidden fat, but it is not known which one he ate; [or:] his wife and his sister were with him in the house, and he thought he had relations with his wife, but they had switched, and he did not know the next day which of them he had relations with, since they were both in the bed and he did not know - he brings a suspended guilt-offering to protect him from suffering, until it becomes known to him [whether he sinned]; if he definitely sinned, he brings a sin-offering. And the Gemara challenges: But is this not something which is not [subject to being] vowed or pledged, and one who sees [it] knows that there is nothing to what he says, since there is no such thing as a "suspended guilt-offering" unless he was [in fact] obligated, and that fact becomes known? And the Gemara challenges the case of the Paschal offering as well.

Rashi on Chullin 41b:8:4.hebrew: ור' שמעון מכשיר - לא חייש למראית העין:
Rashi on Chullin 41b:8:4.english: And Rabbi Shimon deems it fit - He is not concerned about [how it] appears.

Rashi on Chullin 41b:9:1.hebrew: אשם ודאי - אשם גזילות, דהיינו נשבע לשקר לכפירת ממון, אשם מעילות, אשם שפחה חרופה. ועל שם שאשם תלוי בא על ספיקו, קרי להו להני אשם ודאי:
Rashi on Chullin 41b:9:1.english: A definite guilt-offering - [This includes:] the guilt-offering for robbery, i.e., one who swears falsely to deny a monetary claim; the guilt-offering for misuse of consecrated property; and the guilt-offering of a betrothed slave-woman. And since the suspended guilt-offering comes on account of a doubt, these [other guilt-offerings] are called "definite guilt-offerings."

Rashi on Chullin 41b:9:2.hebrew: לשם בכור לשם מעשר - מידע ידעי דשקר הוא, דבכור ומעשר מידע ידעי מקמי הכי, דאילו ההיא שעתא לאו בני אפרושי נינהו דנימא השתא קמקדיש להו:
Rashi on Chullin 41b:9:2.english: For the sake of a firstborn, for the sake of a tithe - [Both participants] know for certain that this is a false statement, for the status of firstborn and tithe was already known before this; since at that time [of slaughter] these animals are not candidates for such designation, so that we would say that he is now consecrating them [by his declaration].

Tosafot on Chullin 41b:14:1.hebrew: והא לא אמר לשם חטאתי - אם לא אמר לשם חטאת, ואפי' אם אמר "הרי זו חטאתי" לא אמר כלום, כדאמרינן בפ"ק דנדרים (דף ו.):
Tosafot on Chullin 41b:14:1.english: But he did not say "for the sake of my sin offering" - If he did not say "for the sake of a sin offering," and even if he said, "This is my sin offering," he has said nothing, as we say in the first chapter of Nedarim (6a):

Tosafot on Chullin 41b:16:1.hebrew: אימר נדר בצינעא - ולעיל דלא חיישינן שמא יש לו זבח בתוך ביתו בצינעא, היינו דאית ליה קלא, שרגיל להודיע שלא יבואו לידי מעילה:
Tosafot on Chullin 41b:16:1.english: Say he vowed in private - But above, we are not concerned that perhaps he has a sacrificial animal inside his house in private, [because] it has publicity, as one is accustomed to make it known so that people will not come to [the transgression of] misappropriation of consecrated property.

Tosafot on Chullin 41b:18:1.hebrew: לא שנו אלא שאין לו אשה - מה שהקשה בקונטרס: אי שאין לו אשה, למה לו למתנייה זה הכלל? פשיטא, למאי נחוש לה? יש לומר: אין לו אשה, היינו שאין אנו יודעין אם יש לו אשה אם לאו, וכן "אין לו זבח" דלעיל; אבל בידוע דאין לו, לא איצטריך:
Tosafot on Chullin 41b:18:1.english: They taught this only where he has no wife - Regarding what [Rashi] asked in the Kuntres: If [the case is] that he has no wife, why did [the Tanna] need to teach this rule? It is obvious — what would we be concerned about for her? One can answer: "He has no wife" means that we do not know whether he has a wife or not; and so too [the case of] "he has no offering" above. But where it is known that he has none, it was not necessary [to teach it]:

Tosafot on Chullin 41b:8:1.hebrew: ורבי שמעון מכשיר - פי' הקונט' דלא חייש למראית העין, וריב"א מפרש דלא שייך כלל לר' שמעון מראית העין, דדומה כמקדיש על מנת לשחוט בחוץ, ור' שמעון לטעמיה דמפרש בפ' הרי עלי עשרון (מנחות דף קט.) הרי עלי עולה על מנת שאקריבנה בבית חוניו, יקריבנה לבית המקדש; ר"ש אומר אין זה עולה, וטעמא שלא התנדב כדרך המתנדבים, כדתנן בפ' המנחות והנסכים (מנחות דף קג.) הרי עלי מנחה להביא מן השעורין כו', ר' שמעון פוטר שלא התנדב כדרך המתנדבים; ובהדיא תנא בתוספתא אהך דהכא, ר' שמעון מכשיר שאין כיוצא בזה מתנדב, אמר ר' שמעון: ומה אם אמר הרי עלי עולה לשוחטה בעבר הירדן, שמא עולה היא?
Tosafot on Chullin 41b:8:1.english: And Rabbi Shimon validates [it] - The Rashi (lit. "the Kuntres") explains that he [Rabbi Shimon] is not concerned about appearance (marit ayin). But the Riva explains that the concept of marit ayin does not apply at all according to Rabbi Shimon, for this case resembles one who consecrates [an animal] on condition to slaughter it outside [the Temple courtyard], and Rabbi Shimon is consistent with his own reasoning, as he explains in the chapter "Harei Alai Issaron" (Menachot 109a): [If one says,] "It is incumbent upon me [to bring] a burnt-offering on condition that I offer it in the House of Chonyo," he must offer it in the [Jerusalem] Temple; Rabbi Shimon says this is not a burnt-offering [at all], and the reason is that he did not make his vow in the manner of those who make voluntary vows — as we learned in the chapter "HaMenachot VehaNesachim" (Menachot 103a): "It is incumbent upon me [to bring] a meal-offering, to bring it from barley," etc. - Rabbi Shimon exempts [him], because he did not make his vow in the manner of those who make voluntary vows. And explicitly, it is taught in the Tosefta regarding this case here: Rabbi Shimon validates [it], for no one makes a voluntary vow of this sort. Rabbi Shimon said: Now if one said, "It is incumbent upon me [to bring] a burnt-offering, to slaughter it across the Jordan" — is it perhaps [still] a burnt-offering?
